caveats: Spotify timestamps are UTC; the ledger is local time. Say 'night-owl hours', never an exact local hour.
The Spotify 'skipped' flag changed meaning across years (79% in 2015, ~0% 2017-2021). Do not build a story on it.
About 47% of ledger rows have a date but no time. Only use time-of-day on rows where time exists.
Health rows are tagged 'sensitive'. Keep them opt-in and quiet.
Place 0..Place 6 are anonymised names, not real locations.
Day-level joins use the UTC date of each play. For an India-local listener, plays after ~18:30 UTC belong to the next local day, so treat day-level relations as approximate.
Both files may belong to different people; treat them as one fictional 'You'. Never name the person or label relationships.
corrections_vs_analysis_doc: Farewell contributions: 9 (13 Dec 2016, 22 Dec 2016, 16 Feb 2017, 26 Apr 2017, 12 Jul 2017, 27 Sep 2017, 20 Oct 2017, 10 Apr 2018, 31 Aug 2018), not 4.
'Wedding gift' (13 Jan 2016, ₹45,000) is INCOME in the ledger: a gift received, so it is not part of The Giver.
The '2' pattern must ignore anonymised 'Place 2' tokens. Strict count is 144 entries (movies 8 of 9).
2014 has 23 plays on only two days (7 and 9 Jan). The silence is 368 days, 9 Jan 2014 to 12 Jan 2015.
The Beatles are #1 in 51% of ALL 7-day windows, so 'they come back after every purchase' (R-11) is not a finding.
Movie days: total plays are not significantly different, but The Killers' share is (22% vs 4%). Use the share.
Apparel and hospital 'quiet days' do not survive a bootstrap test; only salary days do.
New: on salary days The Beatles are 39% of plays (see R-05).
The Giver's 'biggest spend was on others' is NOT supported (bike ₹94k, trip ₹63k, TV ₹20.5k are larger single items). Use 'Pocket money x49' instead.
Monthly hours~entries correlation is 0.70 but trend-driven (both grew 2016 to 2017). Daily correlation is ~0.02. Keep the story event-based.
